title: Silkscreen legibility: pull every refdes back toward its own component, subject to silk_overlap / silk_over_copper / silk_edge_clearance staying at ZERO

requirement.source: owner requirement, accepted and recorded in state.json decision 54
requirement.statement: Each refdes must be visibly close to its OWN component, with no silk overlap. On a populated board a 0603 whose label sits 8.6 mm away is closer to three other parts than to its own and is unattributable.
requirement.objective: minimise each visible refdes's distance beyond its own part's pad extent
requirement.target: no visible refdes more than ~1.0-1.5 mm beyond its own part's pad extent, WHERE GEOMETRY ALLOWS
requirement.hard_constraint: silk_overlap = 0, silk_over_copper = 0, silk_edge_clearance = 0, and the whole drc_routed gate stays at err+warn = 0. This is a CONSTRAINED minimisation, not a free one. Zero silk DRC is already achieved on the board you are given; you must not lose it.
requirement.tie_break_rule: A LABEL ADJACENT TO THE WRONG PART IS WORSE THAN A DISTANT ONE. Where two candidate positions are comparable, prefer the one whose nearest OTHER part is clearly further away than its own part. Do not chase the last 0.5 mm into a position that reads as belonging to a neighbour.
requirement.out_of_scope_note: H1-H5 are board-only mounting holes. Ignore them entirely - do not move their text, do not count them in the objective.

cause_confirmed.headline: THIS IS NOT A HANDFUL OF OUTLIERS. NEARLY EVERY LABEL ON THE BOARD IS WRONG, AND THE ROOT CAUSE IS A LIBRARY DEFECT, NOT A BAD SWEEP.
cause_confirmed.library_defect: easyeda2kicad emits EVERY footprint with its reference text at a blanket (0, -4.0) mm regardless of part size. Confirmed at exactly (0.0, -4.0) on R0603, C0603, R0805, C0805, C1206, C1210, LED0805-R-RD, SOD-323, SOT-23-6, IND-SMD_L5.4, SMB, SMC, SW-SMD, CONN-TH_DS1021 and LED-SMD_L1.6. On an 0603 whose pad extent is 1.2 mm that puts the label ~3 mm clear of its own body and often nearer a neighbour than its owner. The larger packages carry the opposite error - offsets derived from the SILK OUTLINE rather than the pads (ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 at -12.955 mm, LQFP-48 at -8.250 mm, SOIC-8 at -6.600 mm).
two_populations: POPULATION 1, THE MAJORITY: labels still sitting at the inherited (0, -4.0), untouched by any sweep. D21 and R5 both measure exactly (0.0, -4.0) - the owner named them. These are wrong by inheritance, not by anything this run did.

POPULATION 2: labels a P6 sweep pushed FURTHER out to clear overlaps, at irregular offsets - C2 at (-0.65, -12.75), C62 at (-2.0, -9.8), R101 at (-0.75, -8.75). reports/place/silk*.ops.json is 9 files carrying 160 move_text ops that took silk DRC 236 -> 5 by pushing outward, and nothing ever pulled them back.
cause_confirmed.both_populations_need_pulling_in: The owner's words were 'they should be as close as possible BY DEFAULT'. Do not treat population 1 as acceptable because it is uniform.
cause_confirmed.why_the_library_fix_alone_is_not_enough: The .kicad_pcb carries its own COPIES of the offsets, so normalizing the library moves nothing on the board. The library HAS already been normalized (lib/EDITS.md edit 8, 31/31 footprints, idempotent) - that fixes future boards. This board must be corrected separately with place_edit move_text ops.

targets.source: scripts/lib_refdes_norm.py (commit 34a2f6d), run on boards/lumina-carrier/lib/aiee.pretty; full JSON at boards/lumina-carrier/work/p8/silk/lib_targets_applied.json and the dry-run copy at lib_targets_dryrun.json
targets.formula: target local y = pad_top - margin(0.25) - text_height/2, i.e. the label sits 0.25 mm clear of the part's own pad bounding box. Local x stays 0.
targets.how_to_use: These are LOCAL footprint-frame offsets. For each placed component, look up its footprint name, take the target y, convert (0, target_y) to ABSOLUTE board coordinates through the footprint's own position and rotation, and that is your move_text x/y. Treat it as the DEFAULT target, then deviate only where a silk collision forces it.

guidance: ORDER OF WORK: start from the normalizer target for EVERY non-H footprint, not from the current position. Build one candidate ops file that moves all ~111 refdes to their per-footprint target, apply it in batches, and only then deal with the collisions DRC reports. That is far better than nudging 111 labels individually, because the target is the answer for the large majority and the residual set is small.

MECHANISM: place_edit.py move_text ops. Op shape: {"op": "move_text", "ref": "C2", "field": "reference", "x": <mm>, "y": <mm>, "deg": <optional>}. Ops file is {"version": 1, "ops": [...]}. x/y are ABSOLUTE BOARD coordinates, NOT footprint-local. place_edit converts the stored local field position to absolute for verification using: th = radians(footprint_at_deg); ax = fx + lx*cos(th) + ly*sin(th); ay = fy - lx*sin(th) + ly*cos(th). Derive your local->absolute mapping from that exact expression (read it yourself at place_edit.py::_parse_board_texts) or you will fight sign errors on rotated and bottom-side parts. Round-trip check: after applying, re-read the board and confirm the achieved absolute position matches what you asked for.

PROVEN SOLVER RECIPE, from LEARNINGS.md 2026-07-28 [placement][drc][silk] - this exact problem was solved once already and the recipe is machine-verified: a greedy solver works if it (1) offers BOTH text angles on ALL FOUR sides of the part (0-deg above/below plus 90-deg left/right - four positions only is NOT enough in a channel), (2) scores candidates as (min(clearance, 0.30), -distance_to_own_silk_and_pads) so it stops paying for clearance beyond 0.30 mm and then maximises closeness, and (3) processes the MOST CROWDED parts first (descending neighbour count within 4 mm) - largest-first orphans the boxed-in small caps.

HARD GEOMETRIC LIMIT, also from that entry: a 3-char refdes at text size 1.0 needs about 3.5 x 1.75 mm of clear silk. In a channel narrower than ~4 mm NO label can be closer to its own part than to the parts flanking it. When you hit that, STOP and report the residual with its number - do not relieve it by moving a component. Component moves are FORBIDDEN in this order (see the oracle note below).

TEXT BOX GEOMETRY (measured, LEARNINGS.md line ~304): KiCad PCB_TEXT.GetBoundingBox at size s and stroke thickness t is roughly (n_chars * s * 0.75 + t) wide by (s + t) tall, and DRC's silk rules are silk_to_pad >= 0.25 mm, silk_to_silk >= 0.25 mm. Compute your own candidate boxes, but do not trust them as the verdict.

ORACLE DISCIPLINE - THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS ORDER. check_silk is MUCH more lenient than KiCad DRC (measured on an earlier board: check_silk reported 12 hits where DRC found 68). NEVER treat check_silk = 0 as silk-clean. The authoritative oracle is the real DRC: `gate.py --gate drc_routed <board>` which must come back total 0 (err+warn = 0), or `kc.py drc` for a faster inner loop. Run it after EVERY batch.

BATCH PROTOCOL: work in batches of roughly 15-25 refdes. After each batch run the real DRC. If a batch regresses (any new silk_overlap / silk_over_copper / silk_edge_clearance, or any new error at all), do NOT abandon the batch - BISECT it: re-apply the half that was clean, re-solve the offenders with a larger clearance margin, and re-check. Keep a running record of which refs are settled so you never re-move a settled one.

SILK OWNERSHIP TRAP: a check_silk violation's `refs` field names the PAD's owner, not the SILK's owner. Attribute the offending silk to its own footprint before blaming a part. DRC's silk messages are the reliable attribution.

SCOPE - COMPONENT MOVES ARE FORBIDDEN. This board is fully routed (~3089 segments) and drc_routed is at 0/0. `gate place` and check_decoupling are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to routed copper - a prior fix on this board passed BOTH of them and still introduced a SHORTING_ITEMS by moving one 0402 by 0.3 mm. You may move ONLY silkscreen TEXT (the `reference` field, and `value` only if it is visible and in the way). No `place` / `move` / `rotate` / `flip` ops. No copper edits. No footprint-internal silk edits.
DO NOT hide a refdes to satisfy the objective. All 116 are currently visible and must stay visible.

MEASURE BEFORE AND AFTER with the same tool so the numbers are comparable: `python boards/lumina-carrier/work/refdes_prox.py <board.kicad_pcb>` writes JSON to stdout. Before-file already exists (see baseline_measured.file). Write the after-file to boards/lumina-carrier/work/p8/silk/refdes_after.json.

THIS BOARD'S SILK RULES ARE LOOSER THAN THE GENERIC RECIPE ASSUMES - read them yourself and exploit them. .kicad_pro design_settings.rules.min_silk_clearance = 0.0, so silk_overlap and silk_over_copper fire on ACTUAL overlap, not on a 0.25 mm gap. The LEARNINGS recipe's 'silk-pad >= 0.25, silk-silk >= 0.25' figures came from a different board's setup. Verify the live values before you size your clearance margin - you have more room here than that recipe implies, which is exactly why the normalizer's 0.25 mm pad-edge margin is a realistic target.

BOTTOM-SIDE AND ROTATED PARTS: mirrored_text_on_front_layer and nonmirrored_text_on_back_layer are BOTH enabled as warnings and drc_routed fails on warnings, so do not change a text's layer or mirroring - move position only. For a rotated footprint the local (0, target_y) offset must be rotated into the board frame; derive the transform from place_edit.py::_parse_board_texts and round-trip verify, do not hand-guess the signs.
RENDER at the end: `render.py` for top and bottom PNG so the orchestrator can show the owner what changed. Put them in boards/lumina-carrier/reports/render_silk/.
report_numbers_required: count_beyond_extent_over_1mm before -> after (out of 116, excluding H1-H5 from the objective)
the residual list: every ref still more than 1.5 mm beyond its own extent, each with its number and the one-line geometric reason it could not come closer
drc_routed total after the final batch (must be 0)
count of refs where the tie_break_rule (ambiguity) drove the choice rather than pure distance
termination: Return the fixer output contract. Do not start other phases' work.
